title: Q-Transformer: Scalable Offline Reinforcement Learning via Autoregressive Q-Functions
layout_note: Column-per-dimension stacks laid out along a horizontal time axis: within a column the reading is bottom-to-top (token, bins, target), across columns left-to-right (dimension, then environment step), ending in a Monte-Carlo return box that loops back over the top.
grouping: No containers: the update is organised as columns, one per action dimension, each a vertical stack of action-bin cells above a light-grey token square. Thin vertical dashed lines split the columns of environment step t from those of step t+1 and from the Monte-Carlo return at T. A bottom band of long grey rounded bars labelled t, t + 1 and T (environment steps) sits under the token row (Q-Transformer steps), and a long grey arrow axis under everything carries the two phase captions. A three-entry legend sits top right in a dotted rounded box.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded squares, no shadows. Bin cells are coloured by role: green = target Q-value of the dataset action, red with a white '->0' glyph = unobserved actions pushed to zero, pale yellow = the maximum Q-value carried from the next dimension; vertical and diagonal dot runs elide bins and columns. Small grey 'max' boxes with thin grey elbow arrows route each dimension's maximum back into the previous column. At t+1 a yellow cell runs through circled operators (dot product, plus) and outlined boxes gamma and R_t; at T an outlined rounded box MC_{t:T} feeds a long line back to the max boxes. The state history is a small stack of camera photos at bottom left labelled s_{t-w:t} in italic math. A left brace groups the bins (Discrete action bins).
proposed_highlight: The method's distinctive targets are the coloured cells themselves (green, red ->0, yellow max), decoded in the legend; everything structural (tokens, time bars, max boxes) stays light grey.
lesson: Keep two time scales apart by stacking them: per-dimension token columns above, environment steps as grey bars on an axis beneath, with dashed vertical rules where one environment step ends - and colour the cells only by their role in the target.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page ('7th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2023)'). elements 'other' = the '->0' arrow glyph in the red cells. A user-layer card of this paper's Figure 3 exists; this is Figure 2. The whole figure is embedded in the PDF as one raster covering the crop, so measured photo_share is null and the palette is taken over the whole figure, robot-scene photos included.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: robot offline RL with per-dimension autoregressive Q-values
taxonomy.note: Q-Transformer itself; paradigm closest listed sequence-model RL

insights.structure: One column per action dimension, each a vertical stack of discretised bin cells over a grey token square, grouped into environment steps t, t+1 and T by vertical dashed separators and grey bars along the bottom.
insights.data: Q-value bins are coloured cells by role: green for the dataset action's target, red with a white '->0' glyph for unobserved actions, pale yellow for the max carried from the next dimension; the state history is a stack of real robot photos at the far left.
insights.emphasis: The conservative '->0' red cells dominate the grid and a dotted legend box top right decodes the three cell colours, making the regulariser as visible as the Bellman target.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside a column (token, bins, max), then grey elbow arrows route each 'max' back into the previous column's target cell; across columns left to right along a long time axis, with the Monte-Carlo return box looping a line over the top back to the start.
insights.avoid: The many thin grey back-arrows from 'max' boxes into earlier columns cross each other and are easy to misread as forward flow.

arrangement.units: unframed columns of cells, one per action dimension, separated into time steps by dashed vertical lines
arrangement.inputs_as: stack of real robot camera frames labelled history of states
arrangement.shared: bottom time axis with step bars (t, t+1, T)
